algorithm: Factor-to-base-unit tables; temperature via to/from-Celsius functions

classes.desc: Converts between units within a category using factor tables; temperature is offset-aware.
classes.name: UnitConverter

data_flow_ascii:
(value, from_unit, to_unit) -> category lookup
same category -> value * from_factor / to_factor (or via Celsius)
unknown/mismatched units -> ValueError -> demo table of results
description_sentence: A unit converter covering length, mass, volume, speed, data sizes, and temperature, with real conversion factors and offset-aware temperature math.
failure_note: Unknown units and cross-category conversions raise ValueError with a clear message; the CLI maps these to exit code 2.

functions.desc: Convert value from from_unit to to_unit; raises ValueError on misuse.

functions.name: run_single
functions.signature: run_single(value: float, from_unit: str, to_unit: str) -> int

functions.desc: Build the command-line parser for the demo.
functions.name: build_parser

functions.name: main

label: unit converter
output_shape: Prints a conversion results table (value, from, to, result) and the supported category list.
pitch_sentence: I built a {topic} with real conversion factors across six categories, handling temperature offsets correctly.

qa.a: Temperature scales have offsets, not just ratios, so conversions route through Celsius with dedicated to/from functions.
Factors are exact definitions (e.g. 1 mi = 1609.344 m, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg); data sizes offer both SI and binary units.
convert() raises ValueError naming the problem, which the CLI turns into exit code 2.
qa.q: What happens on a bad unit?

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} in Python covering six unit categories with exact conversion factors and offset-aware temperature math.
run_notes: --value/--from/--to converts a single value; the default run prints the demo conversion table.
scaling_note: A static factor table; adding units is a one-line table edit with no code changes.
storage_note: No persistence: stateless conversions computed on demand.
tradeoff_note: Factor tables are simple and exact for linear units; affine units like temperature need the extra conversion functions.
